design.repeatedStorage: Trace resets its independently owned output token buffer to Count0, then allocates separate forward costs/pending/source/path arrays. Output storage is idle until backtracking. Full133k-pixel traces reserve about430KiB for these arrays while already holding8Ntoken capacity.
design.endState: For physically sufficient output capacity, borrow its admitted primitive storage: path at front(2Nbytes), then aligned costs/pending/source window arrays(20*min(N,8192)bytes). Forward DP finishes before any token writes. Backtrack into token slots from the array end, preserving unread path at the front; after all path reads finish, move already-forward-ordered tail tokens to the start and commit Count. This also avoids the original token reversal. Smaller actual inputs retain separate arrays.
correctness: Preserve every price, strict comparison/tie, candidate order, expiration/Resolve, path and complete packet. No numerical policy or SIMD assumption.

Tail overlap proof: after k+1tokens consume S>=k+1pixels, unread path length<=2*(N-k-1), while next token write starts8*(N-k-1); all-literal output is the densest worst case. Full random/copy reconstruction checks still required.

Borrow only Count0/CacheBits0storage in the same OperationContext after reset. Check seed against ENTIRE output capacity before mutation, not just live tokens; selected/borrowed seed data may never alias scratch.

Choose borrowed/separate storage from actual physical capacity before admission, never remaining budget. Required bytes=align8(2N)+20*min(N,8192), capacity=8N. Refusal is terminal, with no fallback/retry.

Clear path/source to preserve original initialization, fill costs/pendingMax before users. Account only newly owned arrays; token owner keeps its full capacity charged throughout both phases. Release other working arrays after actual users, output survives independently.

Use a by-ref mutable ref-struct TraceState or another small safe representation to hold borrowed spans and separately owned arrays; avoid defensive copies in pixel loops and dispose exactly once. No general workspace/pool/cache/governor framework.
design.temporaryCosts: Borrowed storage needs explicit initialization and a final overlapping tail-to-front move; ref-struct calling conventions/bounds may cost CPU. Small controls continue separate-array path. Allocation/admitted peak savings are not elapsed-time gains; measure all. No fixed fixture specialization.
